---
# iHuman Lab presentation template — see README.md for full instructions.
#
# Quick start:
#   1. Copy this whole `presentation/` folder and rename it for your talk.
#   2. Edit the fields below (title, subtitle, author, date).
#   3. Replace assets/logo.png and assets/background.jpg if you want different art.
#   4. Fill in your own slides below — reuse the patterns shown here.
#   5. Render with:  quarto render template.qmd
#                     quarto preview template.qmd   (live-reload while editing)
#
# Any heading starting a new "##" section becomes a new slide.
# A line containing only "---" also starts a new slide (useful for un-headed slides).
title: "Your Talk Title<br>A [Highlight Phrase]{.accent} Goes Here"
subtitle: "One-line subtitle describing the talk"
author: "Your Name"
institute: "Oklahoma State University"
date: today
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: [default, theme.scss]
    slide-number: true
    transition: fade
    background-transition: fade
    logo: assets/logo.png
    footer: "iHuman Lab · Oklahoma State University"
    width: 1280
    height: 720
    margin: 0.1
    navigation-mode: linear
    controls: true
    progress: true
title-slide-attributes:
  data-background-image: assets/background.jpg
  data-background-opacity: "0.3"
  data-background-color: "#252525"
---

## A [Key Idea]{.accent} Goes in the Title

<!--
  .hook = a bold one-line opener at the top of a content slide.
  .punchline = a bold, accent-colored closing line at the bottom.
  Use [text]{.accent} anywhere to highlight a word or phrase in orange.
-->

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

::: {.hook}
State the core idea in one punchy sentence.
:::

Then explain it in a sentence or two of plain text. Use **bold** for emphasis and *italics* sparingly.

::: {.punchline}
End with a memorable [one-liner]{.accent} that sums up the point.
:::

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](assets/logo.png)

:::
:::

## Comparing [Two Things]{.accent}

<!--
  {.cards} containing {.card} = a card grid, good for comparisons or short
  lists of related concepts (3-5 words each works best). Wraps automatically
  based on how many cards you add. Add .vertical (::: {.cards .vertical})
  to stack cards in a single column instead.

  Add .secondary to a card (or a stat, or a flow-step) to de-emphasize it or
  mark it as an alternate category — e.g. "current" (orange) vs. "proposed"
  (gray), or "required" vs. "optional". [text]{.badge} / [text]{.badge
  .secondary} are small inline tags that use the same two-tone system.
-->

::: {.cards}

::: {.card}
[Option A]{.card-title} [Primary]{.badge}

Short description of the first option or concept.
:::

::: {.card .secondary}
[Option B]{.card-title} [Alternate]{.badge .secondary}

Short description of the second option or concept.
:::

:::
1. Hi, how are you?
2.
